description: OKX public BTC derivatives history: open-interest+volume and long/short account ratio, at 5-minute and 1-hour granularity, fetched by scripts/fetch_okx.py. Distinct from schema/oi_snapshots.json, which is a forward-recorded, multi-source (OKX+Deribit), one-row-per-collector-run file -- this dataset is OKX's own paged history for a single (ccy=BTC) series per file.
source: OKX public REST, no auth: /api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/open-interest-volume (ccy=BTC, period=5m|1H) and /api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio (same params) -- see scripts/fetch_okx.py
retention: the rubik endpoints return a fixed-depth window only (no paging further back -- verified empirically in fetch_okx.py) so each run's file is whatever depth OKX currently returns; data/okx_btc_*.csv (undated) is the live file fetch_okx.py overwrites on every run, while backtest_data/okx_btc_*_<date>.csv, backtest_data/auto_okx_*/ and backtest_data/okx_<date>/ are permanent dated snapshots that are the only way to accumulate history beyond OKX's own window (same 4 filenames/columns, just frozen under a dated directory instead of a dated filename).

ts.meaning: bar time (OKX's own ms-epoch timestamp for the period)
ts.unit: UTC datetime (pandas to_datetime of the epoch-ms field)

oi.unit: as returned by open-interest-volume (contracts/notional per OKX's own convention for this endpoint)

volume.meaning: volume over the period ending at ts

ts.meaning: bar time (OKX's own ms-epoch timestamp for the period)

bar time (OKX's own ms-epoch timestamp for the period)

known_defects: the rubik endpoints do not support paging further back via after/before (verified empirically in fetch_okx.py -- both params return the identical response), so a single run's file depth is whatever OKX currently serves; long history only exists because successive dated snapshots were kept, not because one file spans it
oi/volume unit is whatever OKX's open-interest-volume endpoint returns for ccy=BTC and is not independently re-derived or cross-checked against public/open-interest in this file
